items.title: EA set to add AI-recreated John Motson commentary to FC 27 update
items.description:
Electronic Arts is set to add a digitally recreated voice of the late football
commentator John Motson to EA Sports FC 27 in its November 26 update. Players
can select it in the audio settings. The recreation combines archive recordings
with generative AI; EA said it needed the technology to create lines about
current players whom Motson never recorded commentary about. Motson, who died in
2023 aged 77, was the first commentator in EA’s FIFA football series, appearing
from FIFA 96 through FIFA 2005 and briefly returning in FIFA 19. His widow and
son approved the project, and EA paid the family for the voice and likeness
rights without disclosing the amount. The release is the series’ first use of a
deceased commentator’s voice. Save Our Voices Now founder Peter Caulfield says
people should explicitly consent to such uses while alive. EA says it has no
plans to replace its human commentators with AI. The update also adjusts
gameplay and Career Mode. Highlights: Gameplay tuning: The patch improves
dribbling responsiveness for taller players, makes near-post shots less reliable
by adjusting goalkeepers and shot errors, and reduces the effectiveness of
repeated right-stick flicks. Career changes: The update adds a wage column for
contract renewals in Career Mode and improves calendar simulation and
loan-to-buy signings. It also temporarily disables player-initiated transfer
requests while EA investigates an issue. Voice precedents: EA has also used AI
for some player-name lines with living FC commentator Guy Mowbray’s permission.
NHL 27 announcer John Bucigross has separately said AI was used for some of his
lines. My father adored being the voice of the game, and we are so grateful to
the team at EA Sports FC for this touching tribute and preserving his memory
in-game. - Fred Motson Perspectives: Guy Mowbray, BBC lead football commentator:
Mowbray called the project a “non-scary” use of AI and said it could continue
Motson’s legacy through nostalgia. Fred Motson and the Motson family: Fred said
he believed his father would have wanted to remain involved in projects of this
kind, despite not understanding the technology. (PC Gamer) Save Our Voices Now:
Founder Peter Caulfield argues family members should not automatically authorize
a deceased person’s AI voice clone; he says the person should have explicitly
agreed to the use while alive. Derek Rae, EA FC commentator: Rae said expressive
commentary needs human personality and spontaneous vocal touches, while AI may
be suitable for routine surnames; he said he has not decided whether he would
permit a posthumous recreation of his own voice. Sources: EA is resurrecting a
dead commentator with AI for EA Sports FC 27, years after his last appearance in
a FIFA game - eurogamer.net EA Uses AI to Add John Motson Back in EA Sports FC

items.title: Another Live-Service Game Is Going Extinct, And This One Has Dinosaurs
items.description:
Capcom has had a big year, but amid the hits comes news that its
Overwatch-with-dinosaurs game, Exoprimal, will join the live-service graveyard
next year. The game's servers will go offline next year, making it unplayable
after that. "Thank you so much for your continued use of Exoprimal, a statement
on the Exoprimal site reads. "We regret to announce that service for Exoprimal
will be discontinued as of Thursday, September 30, 2027. We cannot thank you
enough for the love and support you have shown over the years, and we sincerely
apologize for the gravity of this announcement." Exoprimal season passes are no
longer available to purchase through storefronts, and Capcom will slowly wind
down the game over several months. Exoprimal and all its DLC will be delisted
from stores starting March 30, 2027, but anyone who owns it can still download
and play it before the September 2027 deadline. Despite a cool premise and fun
gameplay, Exoprimal never truly took off after its 2023 launch.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MEIkK11k09U "While Exoprimal’s early hours of
repetitive and simple missions will likely drive some people away, its later
surprises are a delight for those willing to give it the necessary time," James
Carr wrote in GameSpot's Exoprimal review. "The escalation of difficulty and the
wide variety of objectives introduced later on in the shooter gives it fresh
life several hours in. Fighting through an ocean of dinosaurs is a ton of fun,
and the variety of enemies keeps you from falling into a repetitive combat
loop." The writing was already on the wall for Exoprimal in 2024, as Capcom
announced it was ending seasonal updates and would rotate through existing
content on a monthly schedule. While that doesn't reflect the entire player
community, Exoprimal numbers have largely cratered on PC via Steam: it peaked at
4,9995 concurrent players in November 2023 and nosedived the following month. At
the time of writing, Exoprimal's 24-hour peak was a paltry 23 players. 2026 has
been merciless for live-service games, with several high-profile casualties.
Developer Wildlight’s free-to-play shooter Highguard quickly lost momentum after
its January launch, Anthem was sunset this year, and New World: Aeternum began
winding down operations ahead of its January 2027 closure.

items.title: Why GTA 6 Doesn’t Let You Replay Missions–It Felt “Alien And Disconnected”
items.description:
One of the first things people noticed with Grand Theft Auto 6 is that you
cannot replay missions, at least not in a simple, straightforward way. GTA 5 had
a mission replay option, as did Red Dead Redemption II, so why doesn't GTA 6?
Senior design director Scott Butchard told Kotaku that Rockstar "certainly"
considered a mission replay feature "early on in development." However, Butchard
said, "As the game came together, it felt at odds with the story we were trying
to tell and felt a bit alien and disconnected." He went on to say replaying
missions "really diminished the choices you had made."
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qQdxbUZqRZ4 While GTA 6 doesn't make it easy to
replay missions, you still can do so by reloading an earlier GTA 6 save.
Something else to know is that if you're in the middle of a mission and it's not
going to plan, you can open the game menu and select retry, quit, or restart.
GTA 6 blasted off with 32.5 million sales via prepurchases alone and around $4
billion in revenue on day one. The game is only going to get bigger and sell
more copies over time, and it's helping drive new PlayStation and Xbox hardware
sales. In other GTA 6 news, the actor who plays the character Mandy has reacted
to people being weird online. Rockstar has also reacted to the sentiment that
GTA 6 is too easy.

items.title: Diablo 4 Is Making Helltides A Hell Of A Lot Easier
items.description:
One of Diablo 4's oldest endgame activities, Helltides, is getting a major
refresh for Season 16. As detailed by developer Blizzard in their full breakdown
of Season of Tyrael's Gambit, Helltides will soon be far more efficient to run
than before. The whole point of the activity is to kill as many demons as fast
as possible, acquire the Aberrant Cinders they drop, and then use those cinders
to open chests for items. Dying means losing half of the cinders you've
collected, but they are also lost when the Helltide ends. Oftentimes that means
having left over amounts of cinders you can't spend, only to then go to the next
Helltide five minutes later and repeat the process from zero. It's been this way
since Diablo 4 launched back in 2023.
https://www.youtube.com/live/zhsLeug_ooo?si=EeprZXb-pEZ_KRiQ In Season 16, that
will finally change. Blizzard is getting rid of the downtime between Helltides
spawning and making it so there will always be a Helltide up in one of the
game's original zones, as well as one in expansion areas like Hahantu or Skovos.
Even better, Aberrant Cinders won't be lost once a Helltide ends. Instead,
players can collect up to 5,000 cinders at a time to be spent on opening chests
within the activity. Additionally, the overall loot quality from opening chests
in the Helltide will be improved and chests can be opened instantly. Those
changes should go a long way towards making Helltides feel more valuable and
efficient when trying to farm gear, as you can now blast demons to your heart's
content until reaching the Aberrant Cinder cap. Just don't die while you have a
full 5,000 stored up.  Diablo 4 Season 16 launches December 1. Alongside its
Helltide changes, the season will bring big updates to War Plans as well. A new
system, War Plans Tactics, will give players more control over what activities
appear in their War Plans, as well as more options when it comes to rerolling
them and the rewards they grant. Players will also have new Horadric items to
chase that will modify specific Talisman sets, greatly increasing their power. 
Blizzard additionally announced many of the features that were added as part of
Diablo 4 Season 15, Hell's Legacy, will be made permanent. Those additions
include the season's capstone dungeons, optional bosses like Moophisto, the
Annihilus Seal, Hellfire Torch Charm, and the season's legacy Unique items like
Stone of Jordan.

items.title: GTA VI players uncover hidden systems, secrets and escape routes
items.description:
Players are finding hidden controls, elaborate Easter eggs and unconventional
ways to escape six-star police manhunts in Rockstar Games’ Grand Theft Auto VI.
Released Nov. 19 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, the open-world crime
game follows Jason and Lucia through fictional Leonida. The game includes
everyday routines and relationship scenes alongside robberies and chases. A
criminal-profile system records players’ behavior, and Rockstar says it designed
alternatives to violence to encourage more restrained play. Some players have
also reported a Chapter 3 bug that can prevent switching from Lucia to Jason,
blocking progress when the next story section requires him. One completion guide
estimates that reaching 100 percent completion takes 180 to 200 hours, while
Rockstar’s gameplay animation director says item interactions have separate
animations depending on which hands are free. Highlights: Completion scope: The
game has 93 story missions, 100 optional tasks, 39 robbery opportunities and 22
bank jobs. Portal puzzle: Operating switches at 12 substations unlocks a hidden
sequence that sends players to a single scene in 2002’s Vice City; one player
said solving the puzzle took three days. Softlock workaround: For the Chapter 3
character-switch bug, Polygon recommends loading a manual save from before the
Port Gellhorn warehouse meeting, completing Dealer’s Choice as Jason, then
saving in a new slot. Map clues: The in-game map marks buildings players can
enter in dark grey and inaccessible ones in light grey. Perspectives: Former
Take-Two CEO Ben Feder: Feder said GTA’s edgy reputation still benefits the
series even as it has become mainstream, and argued that GTA VI could be the
last game of its kind as new technology changes how games are made.
(GamesRadar+) GTA VI actor Lexie Shoaibi: Shoaibi, who plays Mandy, said online
attention can be difficult but that her real-life community and supportive
online spaces help her avoid hostile interactions; she hopes the role will bring
further acting work. (GameSpot) NRC reviewer: The review described GTA VI as an
evolution rather than a revolution, praising its more human relationship story
while arguing that some characters feel flat in the opening chapters. (NRC)

items.title: GTA 6’s Mandy Actor Reacts To The Online “Weirdos”
items.description:
One of the most talked-about characters in GTA 6 outside of Jason and Lucia has
been Mandy, a woman who tries to seduce Jason early in the game. She may also be
a serial killer. The actor who plays Mandy, Lexie Shoaibi, has now discussed how
she got the part and her reaction to people being weird online. Speaking to
Vulture, Shoaibi said she's able to see "more good than bad" thanks to her
experience being a content creator. "There are weirdos out there, and they’re
going to try to bring you down, so it’s important to stay around the people and
the places that aren’t doing that," she said. "It’s easy enough to do, which I’m
very grateful for. There’s enough support in my real-life community and online
that I can say, 'I could just hang out over here. I don’t actually need to go to
the scary place.' I’m living in the positive, for sure."
https://www.youtube.com/shorts/JSJwQthWrZs People have been, to put it mildly,
thirsting over Mandy since GTA 6 came out. However, Shoaibi had no idea she was
going to be in GTA 6 at all because when she auditioned, she signed what she
described as an "incredibly" strict NDA. In fact, she didn't even know what she
was auditioning for. Her commercial agent in New York brought it to her, and she
thought it would be "just like any other commercial audition." From the time she
auditioned until the game launched on November 19, Shoaibi did not know she was
going to be in GTA 6. Instead, she did the audition and recorded her scenes for
a project she knew as "Project Bubblegum." Shoaibi said the notes she received
included being told to play a “sexy ex-girlfriend" and to "be seductive.”  When
Shoaibi finally saw Mandy in GTA 6, she said it was "very exciting," in part
because it meant that Rockstar didn't cut it. She did the recording for Mandy in
2023 or early 2024, Shoaibi said, and now that GTA 6 is finally here and her
role as Mandy confirmed, Shoaibi said, "I feel like I'm living in a dream. It's
crazy." Shoaibi said she hopes her role as Mandy in the biggest video game ever
can help grow her profile and get more jobs. "There’s definitely momentum that I
wasn’t feeling before," she said. GTA 6 launched on November 19 and had a
gigantic debut, selling 32.5 million copies by launch and generating around $4
billion on day one. For more, check out GameSpot’s GTA 6 review and our rundown
of five things to do first.

items.title: Another Gaming Console Price Hike Could Be Coming, Thanks To New Tariffs
items.description:
The US government has announced a new round of tariffs targeting several major
countries, including China, Japan, Vietnam, and European Union trading partners.
Under the proposed tariffs, import taxes will rise significantly, with China
facing up to 40% when the new duties take effect next year. According to the
BBC, some of the rates will be reduced because of tariff caps that US President
Donald Trump has already agreed to, and individual countries could also face
different levies. What does this mean for gaming hardware? Trump's first round
of "Liberation Day" tariffs contributed to rising console prices, but the
Supreme Court eventually struck them down. Big companies like Sony, Microsoft,
and Nintendo benefited from tariff refunds after the ruling, but they didn't
pass the savings on to consumers. In Sony's case, it was estimated to get back
$508 million in refunds from the US government.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4FatSqS3VYY&t=19s The new tariffs bypass the
Supreme Court's ruling by using a different law, Section 301 of the Trade Act of
1974, which allows the government to impose tariffs on countries that use unfair
business practices. The law does require an investigation into specific trade
practices before rates are set. If higher import taxes take effect, console
companies could face much higher costs, and protecting their profits will likely
mean consumers have to cover the difference. Nintendo, Sony, and Microsoft have
moved much of their final assembly out of China and into Southeast Asia,
especially Vietnam, to avoid earlier tariffs. However, key parts like batteries
and power supplies still mostly come from China, and if tariffs on these parts
rise, total production costs for consoles made outside China will go up even
more. Some electronic goods could be exempt from tariffs, and manufacturers
often stockpile inventory ahead of tariff deadlines to delay price changes. But
with rising costs from the ongoing components shortage amid the AI boom and
other global factors, console prices remain at risk. After the June announcement
of steep console price hikes, Microsoft warned that Xbox console costs could
rise again in 2027, and next-gen hardware is also expected to be very pricey.

items.title: Lords Of The Fallen 2 Delayed Yet Again
items.description:
CI Games has announced that Lords of the Fallen II is coming in April 2027,
meaning it's been delayed again. An exact release date will be announced in
December, the company said, and people are theorizing that could mean the date
will be announced at The Game Awards on December 10. Lords of the Fallen II was
originally scheduled to launch in 2026, but CI Games delayed it to Q1 2027
(January-March) to avoid GTA 6 and give the team more time to polish the
experience. Now it's delayed to Q2 2027.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EYYXsH-DBoo For the previous delay, CI Games
said feedback and tests showed that there are “meaningful opportunities”
available to “further refine and strengthen the overall experience” with more
time. Despite its name, Lords of the Fallen 2 is actually the third game in the
series, following Lord of the Fallen (2014) and Lords of the Fallen (2023).
Based in Poland, CI Games is also known for the Sniper: Ghost Warrior series,
the latest entry being 2021's Sniper Ghost Warrior Contracts 2.

items.title: Sony’s December PlayStation Plus lineup includes Tony Hawk, Dragon Ball and Amnesia
items.description:
Sony has announced three games for PlayStation Plus members to claim from
December 1 through January 4: Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 3+4 and Dragon Ball
Xenoverse 2 for PS4 and PS5, plus Amnesia: The Bunker for PS4. Members across
the Essential, Extra and Premium tiers can claim the games and continue playing
them while their subscriptions remain active. The selection spans a
skateboarding remake, a Dragon Ball action role-playing game and a World War I
survival-horror game. Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 3+4 combines levels from the third
and fourth games with new parks and expanded creation tools, while Xenoverse 2
lets players build a character and battle online. In Amnesia, players scavenge
and craft supplies while a threat reacts to their actions and sounds.
Subscribers can still add November’s games—Dead Island 2, Tomb Raider IV–VI
Remastered and Monster Train 2—through November 30. Highlights: Skate creation:
Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 3+4 lets players create and share custom goals, and its
PS5 Fidelity Mode runs at native 4K and 60 frames per second. Raid battles:
Xenoverse 2 includes cooperative Raid Battles against giant foes; the game’s
latest cited expansion, Future Saga Chapter 4, added new forms for Chronoa and
Goku. Survival tactics: Amnesia: The Bunker starts players with a revolver
containing one bullet; randomized events and the creature’s unpredictable
behavior can make each playthrough different. Sources: PlayStation Plus Monthly

items.content:
Sony has announced three games for PlayStation Plus members to claim from
December 1 through January 4: Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 3+4 and Dragon Ball
Xenoverse 2 for PS4 and PS5, plus Amnesia: The Bunker for PS4. Members across
the Essential, Extra and Premium tiers can claim the games and continue playing
them while their subscriptions remain active. The selection spans a
skateboarding remake, a Dragon Ball action role-playing game and a World War I
survival-horror game. Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 3+4 combines levels from the third
and fourth games with new parks and expanded creation tools, while Xenoverse 2
lets players build a character and battle online. In Amnesia, players scavenge
and craft supplies while a threat reacts to their actions and sounds.
Subscribers can still add November’s games—Dead Island 2, Tomb Raider IV–VI
Remastered and Monster Train 2—through November 30.

 * Skate creation: Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater 3+4 lets players create and share
   custom goals, and its PS5 Fidelity Mode runs at native 4K and 60 frames per
   second.
 * Raid battles: Xenoverse 2 includes cooperative Raid Battles against giant
   foes; the game’s latest cited expansion, Future Saga Chapter 4, added new
   forms for Chronoa and Goku.
 * Survival tactics: Amnesia: The Bunker starts players with a revolver
   containing one bullet; randomized events and the creature’s unpredictable
   behavior can make each playthrough different.

items.title: PlayStation Plus Free Games For December 2026 Revealed
items.description:
PlayStation has revealed this month's batch of free games for PlayStation Plus
subscribers. All PS Plus members will be able to claim a trio of freebies
starting December 1--Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 3+4, Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2, and
Amnesia: The Bunker. If you haven't claimed November's PlayStation Plus free
games yet, make sure to do so before next Tuesday. Like the previous compilation
of classic skateboarding games, Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 3+4 remakes the classic
third and fourth games in the series. With enhanced visuals, familiar gameplay,
and a killer soundtrack, it also adds extra content to the mix--and yes, the
soundtrack still slaps. While Dragon Ball Xenoverse 3 won't be out until late
next year, don't sleep on the first sequel. It's still a solid action-RPG where
you craft your own custom fighter to join Trunks and the Time Squad, and it
received a ton of post-launch support that stretched for years. The game also
received a free current-gen update in 2024, sharpening its visuals for modern
systems. Finally, Amnesia: The Bunker is a pretty great horror game to play in
case you need to escape all the festive season cheer. As French soldier Henri
Clément, trench warfare takes on a terrifying new form as you're hunted by
sinister forces in the shadows, and the game keeps you on your toes as you try
to escape the battlefields of World War 1 in one piece. PlayStation Plus
December 2026 monthly free games Available December 1 – January 4, 2027. Tony
Hawk's Pro Skater 3+4 (PS5, PS4) Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2 (PS5, ps4) Amnesia: The
Bunker (PS5)

items.title: PS5 And Xbox Series X|S Console Sales Surged Just Before GTA 6 Came Out
items.description:
Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally here, and to play the game natively,
you need a PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X|S. Unsurprisingly, new data shows that
PlayStation and Xbox console sales surged in the week before release. According
to Circana's Mat Piscatella, there was a "significant surge" in hardware sales
in the US for the week that ended November 14. PS5 sales were >2.4x the same
week last year, while Xbox Series X|S sales increased by >2.3x.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ble-JJxBBGA GTA 6 is not available on Switch 2,
but that console saw a 40% surge in sales compared to the same week in 2025.
Before launch, Piscatella said GTA 6 should help boost PS5 and Xbox Series X|S
sales, but maybe not so dramatically due to the astronomical cost of a new
console. To help save money, you could buy an Xbox One and stream GTA 6.
Alternatively, people have discovered that you can stream the game to a
PlayStation Portal device. GTA 6 launched on November 19 and had a gigantic
debut, selling 32.5 million copies by launch and generating around $4 billion on
day one. For more, check out GameSpot’s GTA 6 review and our rundown of five
things to do first.

items.title: Is GTA 6 Too Easy? Rockstar Weighs In
items.description:
Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally here, and one of the things people are talking
about is the game's difficulty level. Some are saying it's too easy. Rockstar
boss Rob Nelson has now entered the conversation, telling Destructoid that
Rockstar's data showed that GTA 4 was "a little too punishing in places" and GTA
5 was "perhaps too easy." So with GTA 6, the team trying to "land somewhere in
the middle." GTA 6 has no defined difficulty levels, which is in keeping with
the franchise's tradition. That said, players can adjust things like aiming
controls, while players can unlock cheat codes to make the game easier or
harder. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dJDf76QVv70 Design producer Scott
Mitchell, meanwhile, said the fail states in GTA 6 were designed to feel
"appropriate." “We wanted to keep things open and not limit the players’ use of
mechanics, such as stealth, but we did also want to make sure we retained the
cinematic, high production value, explosive sequences that we’re known for, and
people expect. It feels like we’ve managed to strike a good balance," he
explained. Also in the interview, Nelson said figuring out the difficulty level
for GTA 6 is itself challenging because the designers themselves know enemy
positions better than anyone after playing and testing the game so much.
"There’s a real process in unpicking some of that to create an experience most
players will be able to enjoy, rather than endure," Nelson said. "The game is so
big, and has such a wide range of content that we can really lean into that,
making certain open-world content--compounds and fronts for example---more
difficult, to give players seeking a challenge something to sink their teeth
into as well.” GTA 6 launched on November 19 and had a gigantic debut, selling
32.5 million copies by launch and generating around $4 billion on day one. For
more, check out GameSpot's GTA 6 review and our rundown of five things to do
first.

items.title: Witcher 4 Won’t Be A PS5 Exclusive After New Deal With PlayStation
items.description:
CD Projekt Red and Sony Interactive Entertainment just announced a marketing
deal for The Witcher 4, but that doesn't mean the game will be exclusive to
PlayStation. CD Projekt Red's Michał Nowakowski said on social media, "Just to
be clear: The Witcher 4 and our other upcoming titles will remain
multiplatform." The marketing deal could be similar to the one between Rockstar
and Sony for GTA 6, where GTA 6 was given preferential treatment on PS5 in a
number of ways in the marketing campaign.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=54dabgZJ5YA Beyond The Witcher 4, CD Projekt Red
is making Cyberpunk 2, a new IP codenamed Hadar, a new game believed to be a
multiplayer The Witcher title, and a remake of the original Witcher. On the
mobile side, CD Projekt Red is working with Scopely on a new game that hasn't
been announced yet. The Witcher 4 now has more than 500 people working on it,
and the game is expected to release in 2028. Given that timing, The Witcher 4
likely won't be on a disc because Sony won't support game discs beginning in
January 2028. That being said, CD Projekt Red is promising that The Witcher 4
will have some kind of physical goodies for fans. In other news about The
Witcher 4, CD Projekt Red recently discussed the game in comparison to GTA 6.
"Of course we did look at the game; we did see the differences. We believe
there’s going to be a comparable leap between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4–I
think so, yes," Nowakowski said. "It’s been 11 years; we are working on The
Witcher 4 to make it significantly better looking and improved in terms of
pretty much every possible facet of the game, so yes, you should expect us to
make a much bigger jump between Witcher 3 and Witcher 4.”

items.title: CD Projekt confirms The Witcher 4 will launch simultaneously on PS5, Xbox and PC
items.description:
CD Projekt Red has confirmed that The Witcher 4 will launch simultaneously on
PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S and PC, clarifying that its new PlayStation
marketing partnership does not make the game exclusive or timed-exclusive. The
open-world role-playing game, starring Ciri, remains targeted for release in
2028. The agreement with Sony Interactive Entertainment covers joint promotion
of The Witcher 4 and the availability of CD Projekt’s games on PlayStation and
PlayStation Plus. Chief Financial Officer Piotr Nielubowicz said the partnership
is intended to support the company’s business and financial outlook, but neither
side has disclosed the deal’s terms or which games may join the subscription
service. CD Projekt Red joint CEO Michał Nowakowski named only PS5, Xbox and PC
as launch platforms; the company has not confirmed a Nintendo Switch 2 version.
CD Projekt has not detailed how the marketing campaign will work, and the game
remains years from release. Highlights: Other Switch 2 releases: The Witcher 3
Remastered is available on Switch 2, and Songs of the Past is planned for the
console in 2027. Disc uncertainty: CD Projekt has said it wants a physical
release, but its CEO warned that PlayStation disc availability could be affected
if Sony stops manufacturing discs in 2028. Development teams: As of Oct. 31, 513
developers worked on The Witcher 4, while the Cyberpunk 2 team had 199
developers. All the platforms release at the same time – PS5, XB, and PC. No one
gets left behind. - Michał Nowakowski, joint CEO of CD Projekt Red Perspectives:
Nintendo Switch 2 players: Some Nintendo-focused fans objected that Nowakowski’s
“no one gets left behind” assurance did not name Switch 2, leaving the
possibility of a port unresolved. (Nintendo Life) Sources: Witcher 4 Won’t Be A

items.title: GTA 6’s Fake Tunnel Is A Great Way To Turn Your Muscle Car Into Scrap Metal
items.description:
GTA 6 has no shortage of forces trying to put a damper on your crime spree, but
the long arm of the law might be the least of your worries if you're planning a
successful caper in Vice City. As players have discovered, the greatest threat
to a clean getaway might just be an impressive mural, as they've smashed their
vehicles right into an unforgiving wall that looks like it was ripped straight
out of a Road Runner cartoon. Located in Vice City's Decor District, this piece
of street art resembles a tunnel going under the nearby overpass, and at high
speed, it's pretty convincing--something I discovered to my dismay, totaling my
pretty sweet muscle car in the process. Does anyone have an industrial-strength
magnet so that I can start working out these dents? I'm sure it'll buff out.
It's a delicious bit of trolling from Rockstar Games: the kind of design choice
that would make Looney Tunes legend Tex Avery proud with how effective it is.
Numerous players have been caught out, and this is just one of many little
secrets and Easter eggs hidden in the game. Fortunately, a gas station was
nearby, and my muscle car limped to it for a quick repair. In case you want to
wreck your car, visit this location in the Decor District of Vice City. As GTA 6
prepares to celebrate its first record-breaking week of release, players have
made plenty of discoveries. The Bigfoot mystery has been solved, you can hop
into a portal to visit Vice City during the '80s, and there's even an island
where bored rich people will hunt you. For more on GTA 6, from completing side
missions to finding a tricky location on the sprawling map of Leonida, we’ve got
you covered with our Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub.

items.title: Playtonic upgrades Yooka-Laylee platformer for PS5, Switch 2, PC on December 15
items.description:
Playtonic Games will release the side-scrolling platformer Yooka-Laylee and the
Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition for PlayStation 5, Nintendo Switch 2 and PC
on December 15, adding sharper visuals, performance improvements, two
orchestrated soundtracks and the Trowzer’s Top Tonic Pack downloadable content.
Existing owners can upgrade for free, though eligibility varies by platform:
Nintendo Switch owners qualify, while PlayStation 5 owners must own the digital
PlayStation 4 version. The PlayStation 5 version supports 4K resolution at 120
frames per second. The Switch 2 version includes a 120 frames per second mode
and higher resolutions in docked and handheld play. The PC version includes the
PS5 version’s visual enhancements and additional content, plus a new “Ultra”
graphics preset. The original game launched in 2019, and this edition combines
its visual and audio additions with its earlier downloadable content.
Highlights: Free upgrade terms: Switch owners can upgrade using a physical copy
or the Nintendo account used to buy the digital version; PlayStation owners need
the digital PS4 edition. Level variety: Players can revisit stages transformed
by flooding, freezing or flipping them, while more than 60 hidden Tonics unlock
skins, effects, challenges and gameplay perks. Review scores: The original game
holds an 82 Metacritic rating, and Nintendo Life awarded it 9/10 in its review.
Other projects: Playtonic is also developing Super Yooka-Laylee Kart, which has
no announced release date. Sources: Yooka-Laylee And The Impossible Lair Is

graphics preset. The original game launched in 2019, and this edition combines
its visual and audio additions with its earlier downloadable content.


HIGHLIGHTS:

 * Free upgrade terms: Switch owners can upgrade using a physical copy or the
   Nintendo account used to buy the digital version; PlayStation owners need the
   digital PS4 edition.
 * Level variety: Players can revisit stages transformed by flooding, freezing
   or flipping them, while more than 60 hidden Tonics unlock skins, effects,
   challenges and gameplay perks.
 * Review scores: The original game holds an 82 Metacritic rating, and Nintendo
   Life awarded it 9/10 in its review.
 * Other projects: Playtonic is also developing Super Yooka-Laylee Kart, which
   has no announced release date.

items.title: GTA 6 Modders Are Trying To Vibe-Code A PC Port, And It’s Not Going Well
items.description:
PC modders are racing to get GTA 6 playable on PC after the leak of the game's
complete Xbox build, but so far it doesn't look too promising. GTA 6 publisher
Take-Two Interactive and developer Rockstar Games haven't been sitting idle
either, as one of the leads behind the Project Leonida Discord group claimed in
now-deleted social media posts that they were stepping away from the mammoth
task of getting GTA 6 to run on PC. Project Leonida has also been taken down,
but it's not the only group trying to get GTA 6 running outside of PS5 and Xbox
Series X|S. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ble-JJxBBGA None of these groups
have succeeded yet, and as Twitter user Chasm detailed online, maybe relying
heavily on AI tools isn't the way to go. Dev streams have been full of users
leveraging generative AI tools to do something, with several prompts being
absolute gems of wishful thinking. Here's a snippet of what people have been
throwing at Google's Antigravity, while butchering the English language:
Continue working and do apply ever part of the code make no mistakes You need
todo one thing at a time not a little bit of everything we need all the game
start like the rockstar launch so on that stuff, not in game stuff yet work
faster there has to be a faster way to iterate than this Even with an army of
enthusiasts throwing prompts and cash at generative AI, a copied version of GTA
6 still seems far out of reach. Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick commented in March
that the idea of using AI and simply pushing a button to make a hit game was
"laughable," and he referenced the music industry, which is grappling with a
flood of AI slop to top streaming platforms. "Right now [in music] there are
programs that allow you to put out a prompt and get a professionally recorded
song spit back out at you. It sounds like a song, but I defy you to listen to it
more than once. It's great to send as a greeting card to your partner on their
birthday, but that's about it," Zelnick said. Whatever progress is made in the
GTA 6 PC port scene, don't expect it to last long before Take-Two's lawyers
pounce. The publisher hasn't shied away from protecting its IP in the past, and
takedown notices for any future GTA 6-related projects seem likely. In related
GTA 6 news, you can read up on how the game has given Pornhub a hard time and
how it became the biggest launch in PlayStation history.

items.title: The Witcher 4 Wants To Be The GTA 6 Of The Witcher Franchise
items.description:
There's been a massive gap between new entries in The Witcher series, and for
The Witcher 4, developer CD Projekt Red aims to make it the GTA 6 of the series,
with a noticeable leap in quality. In its Q3 earnings call, the studio says it
has been inspired by the technological and gameplay advancements Rockstar Games
has made with GTA 6--especially when compared to 2013's GTA 5--and hopes players
will feel the same way when they jump into The Witcher 4. "First of all,
obviously this is a call about us, not about Rockstar," CDPR joint-CEO Michał
Nowakowski (via Eurogamer). "But I do understand the connection here. Having
said that, I'm not going to make a deep-dive and a full-blown review of GTA 5
versus GTA 6. But of course we did look at the game; we did see the differences.
We believe there's going to be a comparable leap between The Witcher 3 and The
Witcher 4--I think so, yes. It's been 11 years; we are working on The Witcher 4
to make it significantly better looking and improved in terms of pretty much
every possible facet of the game, so yes, you should expect us to make a much
bigger jump between Witcher 3 and Witcher 4."
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4c1rokekgnY When The Witcher 3: The Wild Hunt
was first released in 2015, it was hailed for raising the bar for open-world
adventure games. Its side-quests were singled out for being narratively dense,
full of micro-consequences, and on par with the main campaign missions. In the
years since, numerous open-world games have used The Witcher 3 as a blueprint,
with notable examples being the Assassin's Creed trilogy of Origins, Odyssey,
and Valhalla alongside Sony's Horizon Zero Dawn and Ghost of Tsushima. Eleven
years later, that bar has been raised again with GTA 6, which offers emergent,
player-driven open-world chaos through multiple systems. The world of The
Witcher is naturally very different from the consumerism-focused setting of GTA
6, but if The Witcher 4 builds on its predecessor's strengths and adds more
nuance to those gameplay mechanics, we could be in for something special. CDPR
also said it's trying to make The Witcher 4 more appealing to mainstream
audiences, but it hasn't detailed exactly how it plans to do that. "Our games
are different, and they require a certain different approach--we just do things
differently than they do. But in terms of the ultimate effect, in terms of
breaking out to the mass market awareness: This is for sure something we
consider pivotal to whatever we're going to do with our marketing campaigns in
the future," Nowakowski said. Currently, over 500 people are working on The
Witcher 4, and CDPR has signed a marketing agreement with PlayStation for the
game ahead of its targeted 2028 release. The studio is also chipping away at
Cyberpunk 2, but after the launch of GTA 6, the game's creative director joked
about canceling it, saying Rockstar's game set a high standard for open-world
games.

items.title: Inside Retro Reset, the "really inspirational" father and son project teaching kids about classic games hardware from aboard a converted bus
items.description:
At first the kids jostle to get to the games that they know. "Welcome to the
Retro Reset Bus," says Luke Stoner as the students push to get to the screen
that’s caught their eye. Sonic on the Sega Mega Drive is the first they see, and
the quickest student to get on board the bus looks triumphant as he nabs the
stool in front of the console. Jason, Luke’s dad, asks him what he thinks about
the graphics – slightly grainy and slightly pixelated – but he’s not at all
bothered and soon engrossed. After a few minutes, though, his eyes keep moving
to the back of the bus where "Jackson is a wally" is now emblazoned across a
flickering screen in seven different colours. Jackson then gives out a chuffed
yell when his code finally works after a couple of restarts. His retort to his
mate appears on the 1981 BBC Micro Model B‘s screen as the other students crane
to have a look. This is, incidentally, the machine that turned a national
broadcaster into a computer retailer (with help from Acorn), says Jason. Read
more

items.title: Mario Kart World players debate whether eight course remixes feel new
items.description:
Players are debating whether eight reworked courses added to Mario Kart World,
the Nintendo Switch 2 racing game, feel genuinely new. The free version 1.9.0
update arrived November 24. The variants change routes or send racers in reverse
but reuse courses already in the game, prompting some fans to joke that the
patch is an “update of 2s”; others said they were not unhappy with it. The
update also adds Feather Rally and Lucky Cat Rally to Knockout Tour, along with
automatic replays of recent races and battles. Players can select the course
variants in VS Race, Time Trials, online and wireless races. Nintendo says it
plans to add more Knockout Tour routes in future updates but has not announced
paid downloadable content for Mario Kart World. Highlights: Course changes: The
eight variants are Airship Fortress 2, Desert Hills 2, Salty Salty Speedway 2,
DK Pass 2, Koopa Troopa Beach 2, Shy Guy Bazaar 2, Mario Bros. Circuit 2 and
Wario Stadium 2. Rally routes: Feather Rally runs from Mario Bros. Circuit to
Boo Cinema, while Lucky Cat Rally connects Great? Block Ruins with Sky-High
Sundae; players must first complete another Knockout Tour rally to unlock them.
Replay limits: The replay menu saves recent races and battles automatically,
deletes the oldest recordings when storage fills, and excludes races from
version 1.8.0 or earlier. Online additions: Free Roam P Switch missions now work
in online, wireless and LAN play, though not in two-player play or events.
Gameplay fixes: The patch fixes cases where racers crashed without obstacles,
could not jump near pillars, or lost speed using Bullet Bill on a Ghost Valley 2
shortcut. Perspectives: Mario Kart World players: Some commenters speculated
that a larger version 2.0 update is still to come, with one suggesting it could
bring content players want and unexpected additions. (GamesRadar+) Sources:

One of the creators of an unofficial AI-generated PC "port" of Grand Theft Auto
6 claims that Rockstar and Take-Two Interactive have already stepped in to shut
down the project, though the fearful work of slop-and-pasting GTA 6 to PC
appears to be continuing in other hands. Titled "Leonida", after the game's
setting, the port is a recompilation – that is, a translation of the game's
original code into code that'll run natively on different hardware, rather than
being live translated by an emulator as you play. It's based on an incomplete
GTA 6 Xbox build of the game, including the all-important executable file, which
was leaked earlier in the week by crypto grifter Cyberleek. Read more

items.title: GTA 6 runs more smoothly on Xbox Series X than PS5
items.description:
Digital Foundry, a video-game technology analysis team, found that Grand Theft
Auto 6 holds its 30-frames-per-second target more consistently on Xbox Series X
than on the standard PlayStation 5 (PS5). The consoles deliver nearly identical
visuals, but the PS5 suffers substantially more frequent frame-rate drops.
Xbox’s support for 120Hz variable refresh rate (VRR) also helps smooth smaller
dips. The PlayStation 5 Pro delivers the most stable performance and sharper
image quality among the four consoles tested. Sony’s “Plays Best on PS5”
marketing highlighted controller features and audio rather than performance.
Both base consoles target 30fps, but demanding driving sequences, crowded scenes
and explosions can cause frame-rate drops. Digital Foundry said it hopes
Rockstar will improve performance through updates, including stabilizing frame
rates on base consoles and potentially adding 120Hz VRR support on PlayStation.
Highlights: Heavy scenes: In a crowded airport sequence, frame rates can fall to
roughly 25–29fps and approach 20fps during explosions, with the standard PS5
dropping more often. Series S trade-offs: Digital Foundry noted weaker detail
and brief audio cutouts on Xbox Series S. Sony’s pitch: Sony’s June blog also
promoted the PS5’s ultra-high-speed SSD as enabling near-instant load times. No
faster mode: The PS5 Pro has neither a 40fps nor a 60fps mode for GTA 6. GTA
seems to operate with matching settings on both consoles, and I suspect that is
hurting PS5 with its smaller GPU. - Oliver Mackenzie Perspectives: Players:
Reactions were mixed. Some called “Plays Best on PS5” misleading because players
may interpret “plays” as a performance claim, while others argued that the fine
print tied “best” to DualSense controller features. (IGN) Sources: GTA 6

Drops Than Xbox Series X Version - ign.com Wait, What? GTA 6 Runs Better On Xbox

stable frame-rate on Xbox Series X compared to PlayStation 5 - eurogamer.net

items.title: Capcom sets September 2027 shutdown for online dinosaur shooter Exoprimal
items.description:
Capcom will shut down its online-only dinosaur shooter Exoprimal on September
29, 2027, making the game unplayable even for owners. The game and its
downloadable content will leave digital stores on March 30, 2027; owners can
still download and play it until the servers close, while Survival Pass premium
tiers are already unavailable. Exoprimal combines team-based combat against
dinosaur hordes with competition between players. Because it has no offline
mode, neither a digital copy nor a physical disc will preserve access after
service ends. Capcom thanked players and apologized for the announcement but did
not give a reason for ending the service. Highlights: Launch audience: Exoprimal
drew nearly a million players soon after launch, though it did not sustain a
large long-term audience. Match format: Each match pits two five-player teams
against dinosaur waves and rival objectives, with exosuits assigned to Assault,
Support or Tank roles. Current audience: SteamDB showed a peak of 23 concurrent
Exoprimal players during the 24 hours before PC Gamer's report, though console
players are not included in that figure. Perspectives: Exoprimal fans: Some
players responding to the shutdown called for Capcom to make the game
free-to-play or add an offline mode so it could remain accessible after server
closure. (TheGamer) Sources: Capcom's sci-fi dinosaur shooter Exoprimal is

items.title: Just Like GTA 6, The Witcher 4 Has A PlayStation Deal
items.description:
CD Projekt Red has announced that just today, November 24, the Polish studio
signed new deals with Sony Interactive Entertainment for The Witcher 4's
upcoming marketing campaign, among other efforts. CFO Piotr Nielubowicz told
investors that the deals cover CD Projekt Red's games on PlayStation and in the
PlayStation Plus catalog, as well as "our collaboration during the upcoming
Witcher 4 marketing campaign." “This cooperation will support our business and
financial outlook in this and future years," he said, according to VGC.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=54dabgZJ5YA No specifics were made available,
but the partnership for The Witcher 4's marketing campaign has people theorizing
that it could be similar to Rockstar's co-marketing deal with Sony for GTA 6.
Under that agreement, GTA 6 was marketed as a game that "plays best on PS5,"
even if the jury is out on that being true. Sony also created special GTA 6
DualSense controllers and even custom consoles for NBA players. The PlayStation
branding was prioritized over Xbox to give people the impression that they
should get it on PlayStation. The Witcher 4 is in the works now and is expected
to launch in 2028 for console and PC. The game kicks off a new trilogy of The
Witcher games, which will also include The Witcher 5 and The Witcher 6. These
will all be released within a six-year window, so the whole new trilogy could be
out by 2034. The studio is “targeting” a 2028 release for The Witcher 4, so it
could be delayed like The Witcher 3 and Cyberpunk 2077 were before it.

items.title: WoW: Forever’s Best Buffs Now Work As Intended
items.description:
World of Warcraft: Forever players will now be able to get even more benefit
from the game's strongest buffs, as developer Blizzard's latest hotfix has made
World Buffs persist across loading screens as intended. World Buffs are powerful
stat-boosting effects granted to players in a particular area for certain
events. The most common World Buff players see is Warchief's Blessing on the
Horde and the new Might of Stormwind for the Alliance, which are granted to all
players in Orgrimmar, Stormwind, and their surrounding low-level zones when
players on their respective faction turn in a specific high-level quest. Now
that players are reaching endgame and turning in the required quest, these buffs
are popping off constantly. They grant a whopping 300 hit points, 15% melee
haste, and 10 mana regen per five seconds for one hour. At lower levels, those
are some serious stats, particularly the 300 HP. Unfortunately, players haven't
been able to take full advantage of the buffs, as a bug was causing them to be
lost when hitting a loading screen. That meant any time a group stepped into a
dungeon or took a boat or zeppelin to a new location, their World Buffs would be
removed. That has finally been fixed in the latest update, so players can now
enter dungeons with World Buffs to help maximize their damage and health. This
should be particularly useful for doing dungeons at a slightly lower level than
is intended, as the extra HP and melee haste is definitely noticable. Blizzard
clarified in the patch notes that World Buffs will still be removed when
entering raids, so players won't be able to stack as many World Buffs as
possible before raid night, as was the case in previous versions of classic
WoW.  Other changes found in the patch notes include a fix for an Uldaman boss
that players were exploiting to make fast gold. Another is a fix for "a few
spells and abilities" that were causing more weapon-proc effects than intended,
likely nerfing the DPS of whatever classes were taking advantage of the bug. You
can read the full patch notes below. Blizzard recently outlined in the latest
episode of the WoW: Forever podcast how it wants to get rid of the idea of
"best-in-slot gear," as well as how the game's has overhauled old-school WoW's
player-vs.-player systems. In other Forever news, the game's launch has seen
more than 15 million characters created so far, with the highest weekly player
numbers for WoW in 15 years.  WoW: Forever November 23 Hotfix Patch Notes
Classes Druid The 4-piece Feralheart set for Druids now correctly grants 4
Energy regeneration every 1 second for 5 seconds. Priest Mind Vision should no
longer proc effects. Shadow Fixed an issue where Dark Inspiration was not
granting the correct amount of %Spirit increase if Mind Flay was used to
activate it. Fixed an issue where Chastise was not usable in Shadowform. Warlock
Destruction Fixed an issue where Intensity was not working on Incinerate.
Warrior Fixed an issue where players could have and use Mortal Strike from their
spellbook, even without the Mortal Strike talent. This does not remove it from
their spellbook but prevents it from being used without the talent point spent.
Dungeons Uldaman The Obsidian Sentinel drops loot as intended. Items The
Filcher’s Cowl no longer has a level requirement. Professions Cooking Boiled
Clams, Clam Chowder, Goblin Deviled Clams, Giant Clam Scorcho, Undermine Clam
Chowder, and Clam Linguine each now offer the correct Well Fed bonuses and have
been recategorized in the recipe list under “Stamina Food”. Murloc Fin Soup has
had its recovery and Well-Fed amounts increased to the next tier of food,
bringing it closer to other food of that level. Engineering Fixed a bug that
caused Goblin Engineer’s Renewal Gift and Gnome Engineer’s Renewal Gift to
appear as broken, unusable question marks in the inventory. Fixed a bug that
prevented “The Mortar: Reloaded” recipe from being learned upon learning the
“Goblin Mortar” recipe. Leatherworking Fixed a bug that prevented Pattern:
Centaur Hoofwarmers from being learnable. Quests Riverglades - Dunston Willis
once again runs near the end of the escort “Dunston Checks Out.” Wetlands -
After further study, the quest “For Further Study” now has rewards. Wetlands -
The quest “Uncovering the Past” now rewards Ironforge reputation. Wetlands - The
quest “Gleaning Our Future” now rewards Ironforge reputation. Races Fixed an
issue where Wisp Form could be applied to players while they were alive. Spells
Fixed an issue where a few spells and abilities were causing more weapon procs
than intended. Fixed an issue where World Buffs would fall off when changing
areas. They will still fall off when entering raid instances. Fixed an issue
where Fengus’ Ferocity was granting twice as much Spell Power as intended. Fixed
an issue where Darkmoon Faire buffs were granting twice as much power as
intended.

items.title: Witcher 4 Has Fewer People Working On It Than It Did 3 Months Ago, But Just Barely
items.description:
As part of CD Projekt's latest earnings report, the Polish developer revealed
new information about its projects and headcount. For the quarter that ended on
October 31, The Witcher 4 was the company's biggest project by headcount, with
513 people working on it. That's down from 519 people for the quarter that ended
on July 31. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=54dabgZJ5YA&rco=1 For comparison,
the number of developers on Cyberpunk 2 rose from 184 to 199 and staffers on the
new IP codenamed Hadar jumped from 33 to 34. The codename Sirius game, believed
to be a multiplayer The Witcher game, saw its development staff shrink from 84
to 60; the project has undergone numerous shifts throughout its development as
CD Projekt reworks the experience. CD Projekt's total development headcount rose
from 1,045 to 1,051. CD Projekt's overall development headcount rose to 1,051
people. In terms of money, CD Projekt reported Q3 revenue of 208 million PLN
($51 million USD) and net earnings of 109 million PLN ($26.8 million). CD
Projekt spent a lot--more than 177 million PLN ($43.5 million) on development
costs during the quarter--but the company's total cash reserves grew by 31
million PLN ($7.6 million USD). CD Projekt has a number of big projects in the
works, including The Witcher 3: Songs of the Past in 2027 and The Witcher 4 in
2028. Cyberpunk 2 is also on the way, but it doesn't have a release window yet.
The company is also working on a game with Scopely, the mobile gaming giant
owned by Saudi Arabia. Cyberpunk 2 was in the news recently, as the game's
creative director joked that the RPG is now canceled because GTA 6 is so good.

items.title: GTA 6 Is Giving Pornhub A Hard Time
items.description:
Not even porn is immune to the GTA 6 effect, as it's just one of several forms
of entertainment that has seen a decline in viewership since the massive
open-world game launched. It's not surprising, given the game's record-breaking
start, with 32.5 million sales from preorders alone. On PS5, GTA 6 is the
"biggest launch" in PlayStation history, and players spent an average of 17.4
hours playing in its first few days--which probably didn't leave much time for a
quick browse of after-hours material. According to Mashable, US traffic on
Pornhub--which I've been told is one of the largest pornography websites, by
traffic--dipped by as much as 15.5% an hour after GTA 6 launched. Paradoxically,
Pornhub traffic had actually been up by 16.5% compared to average days, likely
indicating that people were bored and randy. Pornhub traffic started to
fluctuate after the GTA 6 launch and reached an average peak a few days later.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=i7l7Lu69V_c Thanks to the game's massive
success, we're also seeing the Rule 34 effect on GTA 6, as Mashable's research
noted a 16,196% spike in GTA-related searches. Up to 15 million search queries
were made on November 18 alone, with users searching for GTA 6, the GTA 6 strip
club, and content depicting the co-protagonist Lucia specifically. The
fan-favorite stalker--and possible serial killer--Mandy also appeared in search
results, while Lucia's partner-in-crime Jason ranked low. Thursday Night
Football also saw a big dip last week, with the lowest viewership of the season
so far for a TNF game. While Rockstar's new open-world adventure can't be blamed
entirely for that dip, it certainly must have had an impact, given that the
football game was held on GTA 6's launch day. That effect didn't extend to the
box office, as The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping opened to a massive $120
million in the US, almost triple that of the last film in the series, The Ballad
of Songbirds and Snakes. For more GTA 6 news, you can read up on how modders are
attempting to make an unofficial PC port, how to fix GTA 6's broken HDR, and you
can check out our list of walkthroughs in the GTA 6 guides hub.

items.title: Thursday Night Football Had Lowest Viewership All Season On GTA 6 Launch Day
items.description:
The Thursday Night Football matchup on November 19, the day that GTA 6 came out,
had the lowest viewership of the entire season so far for a TNF game, but the
low ratings might not be due entirely to competition with GTA 6. The data shows
that 12.23 million people, on average, watched the November 19 matchup between
the Indianapolis Colts and Houston Texans on Prime Video. That was a 9% slide
from the Week 11 Thursday Night Football matchup in 2025 featuring the New
England Patriots and New York Jets. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dJDf76QVv70
Looking at week-over-week, the November 12 matchup this year between the
Washington Commanders and New York Giants drew 16.27 million viewers, and was up
17% compared to the Week 10 matchup in 2025 featuring the Las Vegas Raiders and
Denver Broncos. Due to the poor ratings of the November 19 TNF game, the
full-season average now for TNF games this season sank to 16.62 million on per
game. One expert told GameSpot that live sports like football probably won't be
too heavily impacted by GTA 6 because people want to watch in real time. The low
ratings for the November 19 matchup could be partially attributable to
competition with GTA 6, but a likelier scenario is that people tuned out because
it was a boring game in which the heavily favored Texans throttled the Colts by
a score of 26-3. The Texans were up 17-3 at the half, and the game only had nine
more points total scored in the second half--all by the Texans. Not exactly
thrilling stuff that people would stay glued to. Ahead of GTA 6's launch, people
also wondered how The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, which released on
November 20, might be impacted. It may have been, but the film still put up
massive numbers at the box office that exceeded expectations. GTA 6 sold 32.5
million copies via pre-purchases alone and generated close to $4 billion on day
one. The game will continue to sell, and it should get another jolt of sales
when the PC edition arrives in 2027, as rumored. If you're just getting started,
be sure to check out GameSpot's rundown of the five best things to do first and
our guide for how to make money fast.

items.title: GTA 6 Has A Secret Mission That Feels Like Hard Target Meets Saw
items.description:
In the mood for a little bloodsport? In GTA 6, you can teach one loud-mouthed
hunter that Lucia (or Jason) is the deadliest game, as this secret mission will
require cunning and sharp shooting to survive. It's Hard Target meets SAW, and
the victor gets a pretty sizable stack of cash. Here's how you can be the most
elusive of quarry. Go to Hyde Island Located north of Lummox County and the
Moreau River, Hyde Island is where you can start this mission. All you have to
do is land on the island, and after a few steps, a dart will hit you and knock
you out. Listen to your captor's speech Now for the boring part. You'll wake up
inside of a shipping container, with a fashionable explosive necklace locked in
place. Once your captor finishes his rant, the game begins, and you'll want to
move. Run to the tent directly in front of you You'll have 10 seconds to reach a
tent in front of you, where you'll find a gun and a paltry two rounds for the
sidearm. After the count is up, a hunter on a quad bike will show up, and he'll
be gunning for you. To make things worse, he also has a dog with him that'll
track you throughout the island. Don't engage him; he's heavily armored, and two
bullets aren't nearly enough to stop him—besides, you'll need those rounds for
his dog, Caesar. Sorry, animal lovers. Search for more outposts You can find
more ammo, adrenaline, and a shotgun at nearby outposts. Each one is lit up, so
be fast, be sneaky, and try not to get caught. The hunter is going to be
tracking you constantly, even without his dog, and he has a sniper rifle that
can take you out in just a few shots if he catches you. Prepare for a showdown
Get as much ammo as you can, and choose your spot for the last stand. The
hunter's dog will be a pest, so deal with it first. It's easy to spot, with a
red light on its collar. Trees also make for good cover against the hunter, so
once he's in range, start nailing him with shots to critical areas. Once he
stumbles, unload a few shotgun rounds and finish him off. Collect your rewards
Once the hunter is down, search his body for the Island-Poacher FF-50 sniper
rifle and ammo for it. Head west to the boathouse to reclaim your personal items
and $15,000 in cash. Not a bad haul for a deadly night's work. What happens if
you fail? If the hunter does kill you, you'll lose a chunk of cash and wake up
near one of your safehouses. The good news is you can retry the mission by
heading back to Hyde Island, but the bad news is you'll have to listen to the
hunter's speech again. For more on GTA 6, from completing side missions to
finding a tricky location on the sprawling map of Leonida, we’ve got you covered
with our Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub. This is constantly updated, with
walkthroughs on how to play GTA 6 on your phone, how to unlock hurricanes, and
how to go to hell for a fight against Satan himself.

items.title: GTA 6 Players On PS5 Averaged 17+ Hours During First Weekend
items.description:
Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally here, and it's breaking records
everywhere, including at PlayStation. The gaming giant has announced that GTA 6
is the "biggest launch in PlayStation history, a record that goes back 30+ years
and five console generations. According to the gaming giant, more than 39
million unique players on PS5 have jumped into GTA 6 so far.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dJDf76QVv70 Here is a quick rundown of GTA 6's
new records on PS5 so far (covering the November 19-22 period): Highest number
of concurrent players for any free or paid game on PlayStation, ahead of
Fortnite, Call of Duty, and everything else. Players collectively logged 683
million hours of GTA 6 at launch, with each player spending an average of 17.4
hours in the game's first few days. GTA 6's launch led to the largest number of
newly connected PS5 consoles on a single day since the system came out in 2020,
and outside of the Christmas season. GTA 6 was the first game played on 70% of
new PS5 consoles, which suggests a lot of people bought a system specifically
for GTA 6. A big, record-breaking start for GTA 6 was always expected. If the
game didn't break records, that would be a bigger story. Additionally, GTA 6 is
an anomaly--its success will not save the AAA industry from its many serious,
deep-rooted issues, experts have said, and many believe other publishers will
learn all the wrong lessons. GTA 6 sold 32.5 million copies via pre-purchases
alone and generated close to $4 billion on day one. The game will continue to
sell, and it should get another jolt of sales when the PC edition arrives in
2027, as rumored.

items.title: Lego’s First Marvel Rivals Set Is A 495-Piece Tribute To The Game’s Most Adorable Terror
items.description:
Next month marks the second anniversary of Marvel Rivals, and to celebrate, a
new Lego set is on the way that lets you build the game's unofficial mascot,
Jeff the Land Shark. While we regularly see Lego Marvel sets roll out, this is
the first-ever Marvel Rivals kit, and it'll go on sale starting January 1, 2027,
priced at $50. GameSpot can also exclusively reveal the first images of Jeff
below, showing the completed build alongside his box art. See at The Lego Store
The 495-piece set captures the adorable strategist in all his glory, including
his big eyes, toothy smile, huge tongue, and even his collar. This won't be a
static figure either: once fully assembled, Jeff has a movable head, legs, tail,
and fins that let builders recreate his joyful trot, swimming, and battle poses.
For added touches, his collar includes his signature name tag, his tongue can be
removed to close his mouth, and his fin can be detached so builders can
replicate Jeff's Hide-and-Seek movement ability from the game. "Jeff brings
together everything players love about a breakout gaming character: an
unforgettable silhouette, a personality you understand instantly, and the
ability to turn any match into a story," Lego Marvel design lead Jesper C.
Nielsen said in a press release. "We wanted this Lego model to capture both
sides of him, from the lovable companion fans want beside their screen to the
unpredictable strategist they meet in battle." Meanwhile, Jeff and the rest of
the Marvel Rivals roster are preparing to cap off an entire year of
Avengers-centric events that have been building up to the game's big Avengers:
Doomsday tie-in. Season 11.5 kicks off on December 11. Nightcrawler was recently
added to the game, bringing mutant energy, swords, and teleportation strategies,
and he'll soon be followed by Marvel's unique take on Dracula, who has spent the
last few months hibernating and healing for the battles ahead.

items.title: Might and Magic meets, er, paper in sunny new RPG Rise of Furax, a turn-based island tale that is entirely drawn by hand
items.description:
Literal decades ago, I tried to make a first-person RPG in HyperCard. I got as
far as a fateful town gate confrontation before hitting the cap on slides for
the shareware version. I mention this because new, 100% "hand-drawn"
first-person dungeon crawler Rise of Furax is uncannily redolent of my long-lost
HyperCard game. This risks being a) a terrible indictment of the game's visual
direction, and b) an insinuation that developers Rap2h are dastardly rip-off
artists, so let me elaborate that c) I think Rise of Furax looks far, far
lovelier than my lousy primordial hypermedia confection and d) it is a legally
distinct creation. That unfinished HyperCard concept never left the confines of
a Macintosh Performa that is even now rusting on a riverbed. If only I'd pitched
it somewhere, I'd probably be a MILLIONAIRE by now. A million pounds is still a
lot of money, right? Anyway, here's a teaser video for Rise of Furax. Read more

items.description:
Fine Monday to ya, reader. In the interest of allowing Edwin more time to spend
with his interview transcripts, you’ve got me on Maw duty this week. Not much
chance of it going ungorged, in any case – while the continued bellows of Grand
Theft Auto VI have frightened away most of the air-quotes "big" games from this
late November habitat, many others remain, undaunted. Or because they probably
thought the Venn diagram of GTA fans and grand strategy expansion fans was just
two rings. There’s still some Vice City-adjacent matters we’ll be covering this
week – chief among them the Rockstar North unionisation vote, which is set to
close in the coming days – but as I said to Edwin and Mark this morning, the
cool thing about the continued lack of a PC version is that it leaves open a
space to be filled with other things. Judging by what’s out this week, there’s
certainly no shortage to choose from. Read more

items.title: Nightdive's Thief remaster will make the most "infamous" Thief Gold level a little less maddening, by "just kind of pointing the player in the right direction"
items.description:
1999's Thief Gold is widely considered the definitive incarnation of Thief: The
Dark Project, adding three levels to the Looking Glass stealth sim while tidying
up some bugs, but it has one grievous failing, in the eyes of many: the
notorious Thieves Guild. In this all-new sixth mission, master catburglar
Garrett must infiltrate the lair of a gang of pickpockets, after they filch a
vase he had his eye on. The lair in question is actually very believable, as a
hideout for criminals, in that it resists exploration even with a paper map. It
consists of sunken, samey, obtusely arranged rooms that are made all the more
headache-inducing by objectives that require a lot of backtracking. In much the
same way that I can admire a finely wrought pair of thumbscrews, I think the
Thieves Guild is a clever creation, one that arguably shines when you use every
ability or tactic in Garrett's possession rather than trying to ghost it. But it
very easily becomes frustrating, to the point that many grizzled housebreakers
advise new players to skip the level entirely. The Thieves Guild should be less
frustrating in Nightdive's forthcoming Thief: The Dark Project Remastered,
thanks to a more revealing spread of environmental textures and various other,
furtive adjustments. As with many mods or remasters that speak of boosting the
"immersion", I do worry that something valuable is being sacrificed in the
process. Read more
items.content:
[https://assetsio.gnwcdn.com/thief-remaster_WT2VzYs.jpg?width=690&quality=85&format=jpg&auto=webp]

1999's Thief Gold is widely considered the definitive incarnation of Thief: The
Dark Project [https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/games/thief-the-dark-project],
adding three levels to the Looking Glass stealth sim while tidying up some bugs,
but it has one grievous failing, in the eyes of many
[https://www.reddit.com/r/Thief/comments/4zqr2u/why_does_everyone_hate_the_thieves_guild/]:
the notorious Thieves Guild. In this all-new sixth mission, master catburglar
Garrett must infiltrate the lair of a gang of pickpockets, after they filch a
vase he had his eye on. The lair in question is actually very believable, as a
hideout for criminals, in that it resists exploration even with a paper map. It
consists of sunken, samey, obtusely arranged rooms that are made all the more
headache-inducing by objectives that require a lot of backtracking.

In much the same way that I can admire a finely wrought pair of thumbscrews, I
think the Thieves Guild is a clever creation, one that arguably shines when you
use every ability or tactic in Garrett's possession rather than trying to ghost
it. But it very easily becomes frustrating, to the point that many grizzled
housebreakers advise new players to skip the level entirely. The Thieves Guild
should be less frustrating in Nightdive's forthcoming Thief: The Dark Project
Remastered
[https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/games/thief-the-dark-project-remastered],
thanks to a more revealing spread of environmental textures and various other,
furtive adjustments. As with many mods or remasters that speak of boosting the
"immersion", I do worry that something valuable is being sacrificed in the
process.

items.title: Queen's Domain review
items.description:
Where to start with Queen's Domain? It's tempting to begin with King's Field;
after all, FromSoftware's seminal first-person action-RPG is an explicit
inspiration for developer Freshly Baked Games. But 40 hours later, it feels like
so much more. It's equally tempting to invoke another FromSoftware game: Dark
Souls. Queen's Domain owes an obvious debt to that game's celebrated level
design: the dazzling interconnectedness of its vertiginous world. But that's not
quite right either. The deeper you delve, the more there's something of the
spirit of The Legend of Zelda, a touch of Metroidvania too. Until finally you
concede that Queen's Domain, with its remarkable world of densely packed
secrets, is very much its own. Read more

items.title: I've never known a moment like this in video games
items.description:
It was hard not to spend the first hour or so of Grand Theft Auto 6's launch day
in a kind of stun-lock. As far as video games editorial goes - which is not that
far, in fairness; prepare for an over-flattering analogy - the effect was
roughly the equivalent of Tom Hanks' experience, as his John H. Miller first set
foot on Omaha beach. Tweets and reels whistled overhead, news leads stung the
ears, exploding search terms blew apart some poor guides team ally on one side,
while new discoveries in the early game - made by the millions and millions of
launch-day players all picking it apart at once - appeared by surprise like some
flanking ambush on the other. Read more

items.title: The creator of E.T. on the Atari 2600 likens the deluge of AI-made games to the glut of poor-quality titles released ahead of the US video game crash of 1983
items.description:
At the DevGAMM Lisbon conference this week, veteran game designer Howard Scott
Warshaw gave a talk called "From Atari to AI". Warshaw was behind a number of
famous titles for the Atari 2600, including the classic Yars' Revenge, but
infamously he also designed the game E.T. the Extra-Terrestial, the poor quality
of which has been cited as a factor in the US video game crash of 1983, when US
games industry revenue plummeted from over $3 billion in 1983 to around $100
million in 1985. Read more

items.title: Valve are pausing Steam Machine 2TB orders over "supply constraints," though the 512GB model is free of its waitlist
items.description:
Valve giveth, and Valve taketh away in their latest Steam Machine availability
update. The dinky SteamOS PC continues to have a terrible time with AI
industry-inflicted hardware parts shortages, which at least for its flagship 2TB
model, have become such a problem that Valve are suspending new orders until
further notice. While Valve's post says that they "have wrapped up sending
purchase invites out to all remaining 2TB reservation holders" – meaning if
you'd previously reserved one, you'll still get your chance to buy – "supply
restraints" have put the kibosh on any new orders for now. Read more

items.title: Remembering the back alley brawls of The Warriors, a Rockstar city game that isn't an open world
items.description:
The older I get, the more fascinated I somehow become by how videogames depict
night, how particular technologies at particular times give rise to particular
nightlives. I've already gushed about the Starlight Zone in Sonic the Hedgehog –
the mild dissociation incubated by the soft, ceaseless glare of the construction
yard, the eyeless brick at the level's nadir, the sleepless glitter of the
skyline. Now, let me wind the clock forward, and backward, to Rockstar Toronto's
The Warriors. One long night from the late '70s, sweaty and electric and
menacing, fed through dank and sullen polygons from 2005. Probably the best move
Rockstar made with their adaptation of Walter Hill's film is to retain the
element of phantasmagoria. Both the game and the movie open with a view of Coney
Island's Wonder Wheel, its neon lamps forming a floating tracery of Morse code,
cabins swinging almost imperceptibly against solid darkness. This is a kind of
night in which light is more emblem than illumination, refusing to travel far,
clinging to its source like a frightened ghost. Read more

[https://assetsio.gnwcdn.com/thewarriors3.jpg?width=690&quality=85&format=jpg&auto=webp]

items.title: World of Warcraft: Forever isn't mere nostalgia bait - it's rebuilding the MMO social architecture that Blizzard spent years dismantling
items.description:
I don't play video games regularly anymore. Not because I've lost interest in
them, but because I no longer make the time, the premium on which has seemed to
exponentiate with age. I realised, however, in 2019 that I was a kind of sleeper
agent: whenever I heard the opening notes of Legends of Azeroth, the original
World of Warcraft login screen music, I would feel the reactivation of a latent
part of my mind laid down when I was 10 years old. And so, like a form of
possession, whenever Blizzard announces a new legacy iteration of the original
WoW, no downpayment in time nor money is too great to prevent me from returning.
Here I am, then, at the launch of World of Warcraft: Forever, seven years after
Blizzard first revived the original 2004 game with World of Warcraft Classic in
2019. Once more I set foot on Durotar, to spend as much time as I can levelling
up a new Orc Warrior before I am forcibly unplugged by either my boss or, more
likely, my wife, and so far it's been a welcome return to some of the frictional
- but more involving and consequential - socialising that WoW's decades of
updates had previously sanded down. Read more

shooters in question, mind you. I'm far too cultured for that, you dope! Except

overconfident, mistime how long it'll take them to erode the health of an ogre
midboss, and: bam!

Show me one of those ads, and I'll always watch to the end in the hope that this
time, the protagonist will Study The Blade, conquer their harmatia, and slay the
damn ogre. I've never actually played any of the mobile shooters in question,
mind you. I'm far too cultured for that, you dope! Except that I've just been
playing the demo for Korridor, which is supposedly "based off" of the ads, but
might as well be one of the games they're promoting, for all I know.

items.title: I have double-checked and yes, original 'GTA killer' Driv3r really was that rubbish
items.description:
At this point the tragedy of Driv3r, or Driver 3, or my personal favourite
Drive-thrur, is well thumbed. A familiar litany of unrealised ambition, heinous
bugs, dull open-world design, and an expensive yet audibly bored voice cast, the
accidental comedic highlight of which is Michelle Rodriguez flatly reeling off
car theft orders from what sounds like the inside of a Michelle Rodriguez-sized
tupperware container. A more widely forgotten detail is that, for a while, there
was a non-zero chance - a belief, even - that Drive Three Er was going to be the
opposite. The 2003-2004 hype cycle had sowed the notion that this would in fact
be the open-world crime thriller to knock Grand Theft Auto off its perch, and
even 22 years before GTA 6's idolising reviews, that was no small promise;
Rockstar were still enjoying the balmy success of Vice City, and we could see
San Andreas cresting the hill on a stolen, shining BMX. "Ah, but did they have
Michael Madsen doing doughnuts in car parks?," publishers Atari asked the world,
either unaware or in denial of the spluttering, clapped-out rattletrap they were
about to wheel into the showroom. You likely know the rest, though one of the
dangers of familiarity is the subsequent breeding of complacency, which in this
case can manifest as a thawing acceptance. I succumbed to this myself, having
recently installed a legally unlinkable copy of Drivethreeuh, mind opened to the
possibility that maybe it wasn't that bad. Six hours later, I am here to tell
you: it was. Read more
