items.title: What would Rockstar have done if GTA hadn't taken off? Former tech director Obbe Vermeij on Scottish zombies, James Bond and the "curse" of success
items.description:
It's bizarre today to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't Grand Theft
Auto. Frankly, it's bizarre to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't
GTA 6, which rolls onto console hard drives this week. A decade in the making,
with a development team of thousands scattered across an international network
of studios, GTA 6 aims to be the Maximum Game. It's both a dense, lively open
world and a monument to the exhausting impersonality of "triple-A" game
productions. It contains multitudes: birdlife! Realistic cloud formation! Fuel
mechanics! Romance! Soda visibly sloshing around in bottles! It's an imperial
production shadowed by labour disputes, that appears to have given Rockstar's
various teams little time or space to think about anything else. It wasn't ever
thus. Once upon a time, Rockstar weren't just known for GTA and to a
considerably lesser extent, Red Dead Redemption. Once upon a time, they had a
reputation for slightly dodgy experiments. I recently interviewed former
Rockstar North tech director Obbe Vermeij about a few of them, including Agent,
the unofficial James Bond game Rockstar toyed with before putting all chips on
Grand Theft Auto 5. Read more

items.title: "Games are best made by people": The IWGB and other European unions publish joint manifesto calling on workers, employers and consumers to reject genAI
items.description:
As part of a summit meeting in Manchester yesterday, the IWGB Game Workers union
have joined up with other unions spanning the Republic of Ireland's GWUI,
Germany's GDRT, Italy's FIOM-CGIL, France's STJV, and Spain's CSVI to publish a
manifesto that aims to "bring to light the risks and dangers genAI poses to the
workforce" for consumers, workers and publishers alike. The manifesto states
that "GenAI is currently harming the games industry, its workers and the games
they produce," and suggests actions that can be taken by all to reduce harm done
to the industry. The manifesto specifies the "severe harm to the environment,
the destruction of communities and the exploitation of the Global South" as
wider harms of the technology, but maintains its focus on the industry itself.
Read more

items.title: Break up and re-commodify a fallen Earth in Steel Gullet, a satisfyingly funereal factory puzzler that really loves thermodynamics
items.description:
It's amazing what a difference a few lines of preamble can make to your
understanding of a game. Out now on PC, Steel Gullet is a factory engineering
puzzler that, while notable for its meticulous interest in thermodynamics,
broadly compares to the foundational work of Zachtronics, together with more
recent and focussed conveyor belt wranglers such as Modulus. Resources come in,
and you arrange machines on a grid to transform them into something else, before
sliding them into an output hopper. The difference is that you're doing this
inside a huge walking fortress city, which stamps across the surface of a
largely unseen, devastated and uninhabitable Earth. Your resources are the
refuse of a bygone human civilisation: knots of concrete and rebar, flaccid
rubber hose and splintered plank, that must be separated out before you can
manufacture anything. Read more
items.content:
[https://assetsio.gnwcdn.com/Steel-Gullet.jpg?width=690&quality=85&format=jpg&auto=webp]

It's amazing what a difference a few lines of preamble can make to your
understanding of a game. Out now on PC, Steel Gullet is a factory engineering
puzzler that, while notable for its meticulous interest in thermodynamics,
broadly compares to the foundational work of Zachtronics
[https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/topics/zachtronics], together with more recent
and focussed conveyor belt wranglers such as Modulus
[https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/modulus-is-a-zen-factory-builder-in-which-you-build-pieces-for-other-factories].
Resources come in, and you arrange machines on a grid to transform them into
something else, before sliding them into an output hopper.

The difference is that you're doing this inside a huge walking fortress city,
which stamps across the surface of a largely unseen, devastated and
uninhabitable Earth. Your resources are the refuse of a bygone human
civilisation: knots of concrete and rebar, flaccid rubber hose and splintered
plank, that must be separated out before you can manufacture anything.

Read more

items.title: Star Wars Galactic Racer will get local split-screen multiplayer in early 2027 with new 'Free Play' mode, finally letting racers yell at one another in a tangible space
items.description:
Split-screen multiplayer is often treated by developers as a forgotten vestige
of a bygone age, something to be left behind as the standardisation of online
play makes it redundant, especially following the pandemic. It's considered
unlikely that you'll have another human being in your home to pick up a
controller with you, and since you've inevitably got an internet connection, why
not just use that to connect to anyone in the world? I find there's a unique
beauty in playing something shoulder to shoulder on a couch with another person,
and it seems Fuse Games sees that light too, with Star Wars: Galactic Racer set
to be updated to add local splitscreen multiplayer sometime early next year.

items.title: Microsoft's SideWinder Strategic Commander was a failed attempt to reimagine RTS controls. 23 years later, why are some players still using it?
items.description:
PC players have been conditioned for decades to accept the keyboard-and-mouse
setup for RTS games. One hand has to handle movement and commands through a
keyboard, while the other points, drags, and selects with a mouse. Peripheral
makers have, usually with the addition of more buttons, made many minor
variations to this time-honored arrangement, but there's only ever been one real
attempt to rethink it entirely for the PC: the Microsoft SideWinder Strategic
Commander. Read more

items.title: Spirit Crossing, the new Zelda-ish hangout MMO from the creators of Cozy Grove, understands that sometimes you just want to be alone
items.description:
New multiplayer game Spirit Crossing offers up a visually blissful, but inwardly
draconian world in which other people are not allowed to talk to you – indeed,
not permitted access to the visible electromagnetic spectrum – unless you have
given them a high five. By default, players appear to each other as shadows, all
exploring a skybound landscape of magic animals and layer-cake mountains that
reminds me of both Sable and The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom. Deign to
slap somebody's hand, and they'll pop into colour and be able to join you for
various activities. For example, going fishing, playing instruments round the
campfire, playing dress-up and pulling emotes in group photos, bouncing around
on strangely inflated yaks, or questing forth to heal troubled spirits. There's
some material gathering and crafting, and there are recurring storms that make
the ambience more threatening, but overcoming a challenge doesn't feel like the
point of Spirit Crossing. The "missions" are just an excuse to hang out
together. Read more

items.description:
The tentacles of my trade empire snake up towards France in the west, down
towards Africa in the south, and off into Hungary in the east. Yet, I still
can’t reach out and grasp the throne that sits right in front of me. I’m Marco
Sanudo, and the throne of the serene republic of Venice eludes me. I’ve shed
blood in its name, the blood of someone else named Marco no less. I’ve managed
to avoid punishment for that crime, despite the fact it earned me a fiefdom to
rule while I’ve tried to up my patrician score enough to be the lucky party the
next time a ruling Doge dies in office (or runs out their 10 year term). Sadly,
Doge Leonardo, the mysterious masked lord who’s had an iron grip on power since
the first couple of old blokes to hold the position in this playthrough popped
their clogs, is proving incredibly tough to oust. Read more

items.title: Intel are being sued for "misleading" investors about "a massive glut of unwanted PC inventory" thanks to AI-fuelled price hikes
items.description:
Tech giant Intel are being taken to court for allegedly "misleading" their
investors about the sheer scale of the impact of generative AI-fuelled component
price hikes on PC sales. The class action lawsuit in question claims that
Intel's distribution and manufacturing partners have had to deal with "a massive
glut of unwanted PC inventory", and that the gains from Intel's investments in
AI datacenters aren't enough to make up for slowing sales of PCs to regular
Josephines who just want fancy boxes they can play Deadlock on. All this follows
Intel's last round of quarterly results, in which they announced a significant
revenue fall; this triggered an Intel stock price drop from $92.07 per share on
October 29th to $65.76 per share the next day, which this week's lawsuit
characterises as "the largest single-day price decline for Intel common stock in
over 50 years". Read more

items.title: The Sunday Papers
items.description:
While following a peculiar trail of silver and saffron leaves around the largest
roots of the Treehouse, you come across a hexagonal wooden door lying
half-hidden among ivy and moss. Scraping away the dirt, you discover a faint,
absurd engraving of a newspaper. What mystery is here? You turn the brass knob –
strange, it is warm! – and the engraving of the newspaper flutters. The pages
turn faster and faster, emitting a howling gale that bowls you head over foot.
When you pick yourself up, you are inside a vast attic full of books and
bricabrac, lit from one side by windows that offer no view of the outside world
– just light and mist. Tarnation! You have been lured into the eternal prison of
Sunday Afternoon. Fortunately, there are several ways to escape. Each of the
arcane objects before you is secretly a portal, transporting you to another site
of arcane activity, in a bizarre web of diversions that cannot possibly reflect
the hand of a human curator. Which will you choose? Read more

items.title: The Digital Fairness Act is a decade-long bill coming due | Opinion
items.description:
When a draft of the European Commission's Digital Fairness Act leaked earlier
this week, some industry reactions had a distinctly end-of-days flavour. The
official responses now winding their way out of trade bodies after the official
draft of the act was released are only ratcheting down the tone a little; less
apocalyptic, but nonetheless grim warnings of a terrible fate for European games
companies, muttering darkly about the stripping of supposed freedoms from
players, parents, and everyone else within a very wide radius. Read more

items.title: Will Grand Theft Auto 6 break the internet?
items.description:
Back in September 2025, the launch of Hollow Knight: Silksong crashed the
digital storefronts of Nintendo, PlayStation, Xbox, and Steam, as players who
had waited over eight years for a follow-up to 2017's Hollow Knight rushed to
download the highly anticipated sequel. Read more
items.content:
[https://assetsio.gnwcdn.com/gta-6-headline-launch-gallery-1.jpg?width=690&quality=85&format=jpg&auto=webp]

digital storefronts
[https://www.gamesindustry.biz/hollow-knight-silksong-launch-breaks-global-game-storefronts]

years for a follow-up to 2017's Hollow Knight rushed to download the highly

items.title: Star Wars Zero Company developer Bit Reactor has laid off an unspecified number of people
items.description:
Bit Reactor furloughed "many of its workers" ahead of the release of the
turn-based tactics game Star Wars Zero Company in August, before starting the
process of returning furloughed staff to work in October. Now, it has emerged
that an unspecified number of workers at the developer have been laid off. Read
more

items.title: Help Out Some Bumbling Penguins With This Week’s Epic Games Store Freebie
items.description:
The Epic Games Store continues to give away a free game each week, and this
week's offering is another nice find at a price that can't be beat. Every
Thursday at 8 AM PT / 11 AM ET, Epic offers at least one free PC game (and
sometimes even as many as two or three). All you need to do to claim the free
games is create a free Epic account and enable two-factor authentication. You
have a week to add the freebies to your library before the new one(s) take their
place. At this point, Epic has given away hundreds of free games, and there's no
sign that the program will stop any time soon. The company has also extended its
freebies to Android devices, and you can claim a free game every week here as
well. We keep this article up to date weekly to highlight both the current free
games and next week's offerings. If you're looking for more freebies, you can
check out our list of the 25 best free PC games to play right now, or for more
options, the 25 best free games to play on multiple platforms. Current free
games at Epic Bread and Fred This week, you can get a welcome gift pack for
Firestone: Idle Clicker Online RPG, and you can help a pair of penguins out in
the co-op platformer Bread & Fred. The welcome pack for Firestone is valued at
$100, and it includes an exclusive Talia skin, chests, avatars and gems. New
players must reach stage 15 to claim it. Next free game at Epic Next week, you
can get Strange Antiquities for free. Run a shop full of occult antiques in the
eerie town of Undermere, uncover sinister secrets, help the locals out, and do
pet your adorable shop cat. See all free games at Epic Epic Games Store free
games list We're keeping a running list of every free game that Epic users have
been able to claim in the past. From AAA hits to indie darlings, Epic has really
made its mark with free games. You can even snag these games if you don't have a
powerful PC so you can play them if you ever get one. Look at the list below to
see the frankly ridiculous list of free games that have been available. GameDate

The Epic Games Store continues to give away a free game each week, and this
week's offering is another nice find at a price that can't be beat. Every
Thursday at 8 AM PT / 11 AM ET, Epic offers at least one free PC game (and
sometimes even as many as two or three). All you need to do to claim the free
games is create a free Epic account [https://www.epicgames.com/id/register] and
enable two-factor authentication. You have a week to add the freebies to your
library before the new one(s) take their place. At this point, Epic has given
away hundreds of free games, and there's no sign that the program will stop any
time soon. The company has also extended its freebies to Android devices, and
you can claim a free game every week here as well
[https://www.gamespot.com/articles/free-games-epic-games-store-mobile/1100-6530257/].
We keep this article up to date weekly to highlight both the current free games
and next week's offerings.

If you're looking for more freebies, you can check out our list of the 25 best
free PC games to play right now
[https://www.gamespot.com/gallery/best-free-pc-games/2900-6309/], or for more
options, the 25 best free games to play
[https://www.gamespot.com/gallery/best-free-games/2900-5406/] on multiple
platforms.


CURRENT FREE GAMES AT EPIC

[https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Bread-and-Fred.jpg?w=636]Bread
and Fred

This week, you can get a welcome gift pack for Firestone: Idle Clicker Online
RPG, [https://store.epicgames.com/p/firestone-online-idle-rpg-bfd04b] and you
can help a pair of penguins out in the co-op platformer Bread & Fred
[https://store.epicgames.com/p/bread-and-fred-1db362]. The welcome pack for
Firestone is valued at $100, and it includes an exclusive Talia skin, chests,
avatars and gems. New players must reach stage 15 to claim it.


NEXT FREE GAME AT EPIC

[https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Strange-Antiquities.jpg?w=636]

Next week, you can get Strange Antiquities
[https://store.epicgames.com/p/strange-antiquities-e37660] for free. Run a shop
full of occult antiques in the eerie town of Undermere, uncover sinister
secrets, help the locals out, and do pet your adorable shop cat.

See all free games at Epic [https://store.epicgames.com/en-US/]

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

to claim in the past. From AAA hits to indie darlings, Epic has really made its
mark with free games. You can even snag these games if you don't have a powerful
PC so you can play them if you ever get one. Look at the list below to see the

items.title: Petit Planet preview: HoYoverse's first foray into family-friendly games is very careful to colour within the lines
items.description:
This isn't a complaint, but I can't help but feel like every new game I pick up
at the moment is Animal Crossing. Heartopia? Animal Crossing. Pokopia? Animal
Crossing. Tomodachi Life? You guessed it, Animal Crossing! I am unashamedly one
of those people who thinks the gaming landscape of the 2020s peaked early when
New Horizons gently shepherded us all through lockdown, so perhaps I shouldn't
be surprised that – now that we're well past the midpoint of the decade, I hate
to remind you – a bunch of studios have come to the same conclusion, and either
spun up their own take on the idea, or repurposed an existing IP to include more
Animal Crossing-like elements. Read more
